title: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar

sections.skill: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar

questions.skill: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has angles of 35° and 85°. Triangle DEF has angles of 35° and 60°. Are the triangles similar? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangle ABC has angles of 35° and 85°. Triangle DEF has angles of 35° and 60°.
Are the triangles similar? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. The third angle of DEF is 180° - 35° - 60° = 85°, so two pairs of angles are equal (AA).

questions.skill: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar
questions.prompt: A 5-foot post casts a 3-foot shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 12-foot shadow. Explain why the two triangles are similar, and find the height of the tree.
questions.prompt_markup:
A 5-foot post casts a 3-foot shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a 12-foot shadow.
Explain why the two triangles are similar, and find the height of the tree.
questions.correct_answer: Both triangles have a right angle and the same angle of the sun's rays, so they are similar by AA. The tree is 20 feet tall.
questions.grading_note: Grade both: the AA reason and 20 feet.

questions.skill: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar
questions.prompt: In the figure, segment DE is parallel to BC. Explain why triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.
questions.prompt_markup:
In the figure, segment DE is parallel to BC.
Explain why triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.
questions.correct_answer: The triangles share angle A, and angle ADE = angle ABC (corresponding angles, because DE ∥ BC). So they are similar by AA.

sections.skill: Establish the angle-angle criterion with similarity transformations

questions.skill: Establish the angle-angle criterion with similarity transformations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Which transformations show that the triangles are similar?
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E.
Which transformations show that the triangles are similar?
questions.correct_answer: A dilation that makes AB the same length as DE, followed by rigid motions that move the image onto DEF; the equal angles make the third vertices match.

questions.skill: Establish the angle-angle criterion with similarity transformations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Explain why a similarity transformation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E.
Explain why a similarity transformation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
questions.correct_answer: Dilate ABC by the scale factor DE ÷ AB, so the image of AB has the same length as DE. Rigid motions then move that image onto DE (A onto D, B onto E), with the third vertex on the same side as F. Because angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E, the image's other two sides lie along rays DF and EF, and two rays meet in only one point, so the third vertex lands on F. (The third angles are then equal too.)
questions.grading_note: Full credit needs the dilation, the rigid motions, and why the third vertex must land on F.

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to solve multistep problems, including altitudes and parallel segments
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C, and D is the foot of the altitude from C to hypotenuse AB. AD = 4 and DB = 9. Find CD, and name the similar triangles you used.
questions.prompt_markup:
In right triangle ABC, the right angle is at C, and D is the foot of the altitude from C to hypotenuse AB. AD = 4 and DB = 9.
Find CD, and name the similar triangles you used.
questions.correct_answer: CD = 6. Triangles ACD and CBD are similar, so AD ÷ CD = CD ÷ DB and CD² = 4 · 9 = 36.
questions.grading_note: Both the length and the similar triangles are required.
